label: assertion
text: Applying dynamic sparsification methods consistently modifies three correlative indicators of plasticity in multi-task agents trained on MiniGrid benchmarks.

label: assertion
text: The percentage of dormant neurons (fraction of neurons whose mean absolute activation normalized within the layer is below threshold τ) is reduced under sparsification compared to dense baselines.

label: assertion
text: SET is typically attaining the lowest dormancy levels (fraction of neurons whose mean absolute activation normalized within the layer is below threshold τ) across actor and critic components.

label: assertion
text: The effective rank of shared feature representations—measured as srank_δ(Φ)=min_k{∑_{i=1}^k σ_i / ∑_{i=1}^d σ_i ≥ 1−δ} for singular values σ_i of feature matrix Φ—is maintained or increased under sparsification relative to dense baselines.

label: assertion
text: The trace of the Fisher Information Matrix—Tr(F)=E_{s,a∼π}[||∇_θ log π(a|s)||_2^2]—generally stabilizes at lower or less volatile values for sparse agents.

label: assertion
text: GMP is often showing a peak-and-decline pattern in the trace of the Fisher Information Matrix.

label: assertion
text: SET is maintaining a low, steady trace of the Fisher Information Matrix.

label: assertion
text: Across multiple MTRL architectures and MiniGrid benchmarks, agents trained with GMP (final target sparsity 95% in main experiments) or SET (fixed sparsity 95% with ERK initialization and evolution parameter ε) achieve higher normalized interquantile mean (IQM) aggregate returns than their dense counterparts.

label: example
text: In the MTPPO configuration on MT5, GMP attains IQM = 0.81 (95% CI: 0.75–0.86) and SET attains IQM = 0.80 (95% CI: 0.75–0.84), both exceeding the dense IQM = 0.65 (95% CI: 0.61–0.71).

label: assertion
text: These sparse agents (agents trained with GMP or SET) also compare favorably against alternative plasticity interventions and common regularization baselines in many settings.

label: assertion
text: The effectiveness of Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP, which progressively increases sparsity following a cubic schedule) and Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET, which maintains constant sparsity with periodic pruning and regrowth) depends on architectural design.

text: In the continuous-control Multi-Task Multi-Headed Soft Actor-Critic (MTMH-SAC) experiments on MetaWorld MT10, actor-only pruning (i.e., applying Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) exclusively to the actor network, keeping the critic dense) increased mean effective rank (dimensionality of feature space measured via singular values) compared to both the dense and globally pruned agents (the dense MTMH-SAC baseline and the agent pruned by global actor+critic pruning, respectively).

text: In Multi-Task PPO (MTPPO) experiments on the MT5 benchmark, pairing Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) with Weight Decay (GMP+WD) or PCGrad (gradient surgery that projects conflicting gradients to reduce interference) yields no additional performance gains over GMP alone and in some cases slightly worsens plasticity indicators and final returns.

text: Both Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) and Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) improve correlative plasticity indicators (neuron dormancy (percentage of neurons with normalized mean absolute activation below threshold $\tau$); effective rank (dimensionality of feature space via singular values); Fisher trace ($\operatorname{Tr}(F)=\mathbb{E}_{s,a\sim\pi}[\|\nabla_\theta\log\pi(a|s)\|_2^2]$)) relative to dense baselines.

label: assertion
text: Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) and Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) produce different temporal patterns.

label: assertion
text: Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) commonly exhibits a characteristic peak-and-decline in the Fisher trace ($\operatorname{Tr}(F)=\mathbb{E}_{s,a\sim\pi}[\|\nabla_\theta\log\pi(a|s)\|_2^2]$).

label: assertion
text: Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) tends to reduce neuron dormancy (percentage of neurons with normalized mean absolute activation below threshold $\tau$) more strongly in actor than critic in some settings.

label: assertion
text: Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) produces consistently low Fisher trace values ($\operatorname{Tr}(F)=\mathbb{E}_{s,a\sim\pi}[\|\nabla_\theta\log\pi(a|s)\|_2^2]$).

label: assertion
text: Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) maintains very low neuron dormancy (percentage of neurons with normalized mean absolute activation below threshold $\tau$) throughout training.

label: assertion
text: These distinct dynamics of Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) and Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) imply differing adaptation profiles.

label: assertion
text: Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) promotes staged sparsification adaptation.

label: assertion
text: Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) supports continuous topological exploration.

label: assertion
text: Preliminary experiments on the MT5 benchmark (a multi-task MiniGrid crossing of 5 tasks) show that Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) style rewinding (early rewinding at iteration 1 with 1 epoch warmup to target sparsity 95%) did not produce significant improvements over single-task baselines and underperformed relative to Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) and Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) in multi-task scenarios, indicating that fixed sparse subnetworks found via early rewinding are less capable of adapting across diverse tasks compared to dynamically adapting sparsification strategies.

text: Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) applied in the evaluated multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL) settings tends to produce very low dormant neuron percentages, where dormant neurons are neurons with normalized mean absolute activation below threshold τ.

label: 论据
text: While Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) applied in the evaluated multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL) settings tends to produce very low dormant neuron percentages (dormant neurons are neurons with normalized mean absolute activation below threshold τ), it simultaneously causes a severe and persistent reduction in effective rank of feature representations (dimensionality of feature space measured via singular values).

label: 论据
text: Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) applied in the evaluated multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL) settings causes a severe and persistent reduction in effective rank of feature representations (dimensionality of feature space measured via singular values), correlating with substantially worse aggregated multi-task returns compared to both dense and sparsified agents.

label: assertion
text: Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) can suppress neuron inactivity, i.e., the state of dormant neurons (neurons with normalized mean absolute activation below threshold τ), at the cost of representational diversity, i.e., dimensionality of feature space measured via singular values, in multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL) contexts.
